subject: RFP Clarifications — staged delivery sprint matrix & cutover Qs
messages:
From: Megan Li <megan.li@atlasfs.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: RFP clarifications — staged delivery sprint matrix & cutover questions

Connor / Laura —

Thanks for the draft RFP submission. A few clarifications from our onboarding and ops teams so we can accurately score implementation risk: 

1) Timeline ask: for a pilot (10% traffic), canary (incremental 25/50/100), and full go-live — what are the typical durations you propose per stage (in weeks) and the required customer-side prep windows?

2) Integration touchpoints: high-level sequence for (a) authentication and key rotation, (b) data ingestion (batch vs streaming), and (c) monitoring/alerting exports we can validate during pilot.

3) Rollback criteria: what metrics and maximum RTO do you commit to for a rollback during canary?

4) Operational blackout windows: are there maintenance windows or migration constraints we must plan for?

Please send a staged delivery sprint matrix and any integration diagrams we can share with our infra team by end of week (Dec 3).

Also loop in Rajesh (cc'd) from Atlas IT for any infra-level questions.

Thanks,
Megan Li
Senior Procurement Manager
Atlas Financial Services

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP clarifications — staged delivery sprint matrix & cutover questions

Hi Megan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is our initial staged delivery sprint matrix (staged_sprint_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a simplified integration sequence diagram. High-level answers below; the spreadsheet includes week-by-week milestones and owner mappings.

1) Typical durations (customer-dependent):
- Pilot (10%): 2 weeks active testing + 1 week ramp validation (total ~3 weeks)
- Canary phase (25% -> 50% -> 100%): 1 week at each increment for validation, so 3 weeks nominal; we recommend a 1-week stabilization after final ramp before declaring GA.
- Full GA cutover: 1 business-day switch, with a 72-hour monitoring SLA window and optional 7-day elevated support.

2) Integration sequence (summary):
- Week 0: Exchange keys / endpoint allowlists, establish VPC peering or private endpoints if requested.
- Week 1: API contract verification (schema, auth), small-scale tokenized test ingest.
- Week 2–3: Pilot traffic + telemetry validation (latency, error budget).
- Week 4–6: Canary ramping per schedule in spreadsheet.

3) Rollback criteria & RTO:
- Rollback triggers: 5xx rate >1% sustained over 10 minutes, latency median >2x baseline for 15 minutes, or severe quality regression flagged by your QA prompts.
- Target RTO: 30 minutes to revert to previous variant for model routing; full traffic reversion within 2 hours if infra rollback required.

4) Blackouts: No forced maintenance during pilot/canary windows; scheduled maintenance windows are T+14 days after GA unless otherwise negotiated.

Attachments: staged_sprint_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx), integration_sequence_diagram.png (png)

Next steps: Laura will add technical runbook details and dependency notes. I can walk Rajesh through the matrix tomorrow — available 10–12 PST.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien

Redwood Inference

Megan / Connor / Rajesh —

Adding technical specifics that will live in the onboarding runbook (attached: onboarding-dependencies-v1.docx). Highlights: 

- Auth & key rotation: We support short-lived API keys via your KMS (we can integrate with Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS). Key rotation test is part of Week 0—they should be able to rotate without requests losing sessions.

- Data ingestion: two patterns supported — sync batch (S3 pulls) and streaming (gRPC over private link). For streaming we recommend token window sizes and backpressure handling; the runbook includes sample configs.

- Observability: We export Prometheus metrics + Datadog traces. During pilot we'll verify the three critical metrics: error_rate_5m, latency_p95, and token_throughput. We also set up a lightweight sampling-based transcript check to monitor quality drift.

- Canary mechanics: Model routing is weight-based at the edge. Typical ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%. We implement automated health checks (latency and 5xx) and a webhook to your ops channel to block progress if thresholds are breached.

- Rollback procedure: If automated checks trigger, routing reverts within target RTO and we push a hotfix branch for model/config reasons. For data-layer issues we maintain crosswalked keys for safe replay — retention policy and replay windows are documented in the runbook.

- Cutover validation tests (we run these together with Atlas QA): synthetic load, a curated prompt set for quality regression, and live-sample validation (sampling 0.5–1% of traffic).

Please see the attached doc for dependency versions, sample API calls, and a checklist of Atlas-side firewall/NAT rules. Happy to hop on a technical call to walk Rajesh through the gRPC options.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Megan / team —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Quick executive notes from our side to help procurement: 

- SE staffing: We typically allocate a dedicated SE (up to 16 hours/week) during pilot and a rotating on-call pool (8–12 hours/week) across the canary window. For larger pilots we can increase to 24 hours/week for the first two weeks.

- Historic worst-case rollback: In our largest customer runs, a cross-service rollback (routing + infra change) has taken up to 3.5 hours due to coordination with partner infra teams; pure model-routing reverts are typically <30 minutes. We treat the 3.5 hour case as an outlier tied to cross-account network changes.

- Data residency: We can scope an EU-only pilot but that typically extends validation by 1–2 weeks for legal and data ingestion checks. We'll note this as an optional gating criterion.

Procurement + Rajesh — Connor and Laura have provided the artifacts we discussed. If helpful, I'm available for a 30-minute sponsor call to confirm SLA exceptions and sign-off language before you circulate the SOW addendum. Proposed times: Mon 12/7 9–11 PST or Tue 12/8 14–16 PST.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Customer Programs
Redwood Inference
